At Snowflake, we are powering the era of the agentic enterprise. To usher in this new era, we seek AI-native thinkers across every function who are energized by the opportunity to reinvent how they work. You don’t just use tools; you possess an innate curiosity, treating AI as a high-trust collaborator that is core to how you solve problems and accelerate your impact. We look for low-ego individuals who thrive in dynamic and fast-moving environments and move with an experimental mindset — who rapidly test emerging capabilities to discover simpler, more powerful ways to deliver results. At Snowflake, your role isn't just to execute a function, but to help redefine the future of how work gets done.


SOFTWARE ENGINEER INTERN (DATABASE ENGINEERING) - SUMMER 2027

Snowflake started with a clear vision: develop a cloud data platform that is effective, affordable, and accessible to all data users. Snowflake developed an innovative new product with a built-for-the-cloud architecture that combines the power of data warehousing, the flexibility of big data platforms, and the elasticity of the cloud at a fraction of the cost of traditional solutions. We are now a global, world-class organization with offices in more than a dozen countries and serving many more.

We're looking for dedicated students who share our passion for ground-breaking technology and want to create a lasting future for you and Snowflake.




WHAT WE OFFER:

 - Paid, full-time internships in the heart of the software industry

 - Exposure to a fast-paced, fun and inclusive culture

 - A chance to work with world-class experts on challenging projects

 - Opportunity to provide meaningful contributions to a real system used by customers

 - High level of access to supervisors (manager and mentor), detailed direction without micromanagement, feedback throughout your internship, and a final evaluation

 - Stuff that matters: treated as a member of the Snowflake team, included in company meetings/activities, flexible hours, casual dress code, accommodations to work from home, swag and much more

 - When return to office in effect, catered lunches, access to gaming consoles, recreational games, happy hours, company outings, and more




WHAT WE EXPECT:

 - Must be actively enrolled in an accredited college/university program during the time of the internship

 - Desired class level: 3rd/4th year Undergraduates, Masters, or PhD

 - Desired majors: Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Physics, Math, or related field

 - Required coursework: algorithms, data structures, software engineering, and operating systems

 - Recommended coursework: cloud computing, compilers, database systems, distributed systems, functional PL, networking

 - Bonus experience: research or publications in databases or distributed systems, and contributions to open source

 - Experience working with big data (engineering / processing)
   Excellent programming skills in C++ or Java

 - Preferred knowledge of C++20 or C++17, Java 20 or Java 17

 - Knowledge of data structures and algorithms

 - Systems programming skills including multi-threading, concurrency, etc.

 - Strong problem solving and ability to learn quickly in a dynamic environment

 - Experience with working as a part of a team

 - Dedication and passion for technology

 - Required to work from designated office full time



When: 

 - Summer 2027

 - Eligible start date options: May 10, 2027; May 24, 2027, June 21, 2027

 - Eligible end date options: July 30, 2027; August 13, 2027; August 27, 2027; September 10, 2027

 - Duration: 12 week minimum, 16 weeks recommended (12 month maximum)




WHAT YOU WILL LEARN/GAIN:

 - How to build enterprise grade, reliable, and trustworthy software/services

 - Exposure to SQL or other database technologies (e.g., Spark, Hadoop)

 - Understanding of database internals, large-scale data processing, transaction processing, distributed systems, and data warehouse design

 - Implementation, testing of features in query compilation, compiler design, query execution

 - Experience working with cloud infrastructure, AWS, Azure, and/or Google Cloud in particular

 - Learning about cutting edge database technology and research




POSSIBLE TEAMS/WORK FOCUS AREAS:

 - Various spaces within Database Query Engine (such as the compiler, query optimization, query execution & performance, SQL frameworks, etc.), FoundationDB key-value store (FDB storage, FDB Performance, etc.), and Hybrid Transactional & Analytical Processing (Unistore)

 - High performance large-scale data processing

 - Large-scale distributed systems

 - Software-as-a-Service platform

 - Software frameworks for stability and performance testing



Every Snowflake employee is expected to follow the company's confidentiality and security standards for handling sensitive data. Snowflake employees must abide by the company's data security plan as an essential part of their duties. It is every employee's duty to keep customer information secure and confidential.

Snowflake is growing fast, and we’re scaling our team to help enable and accelerate our growth. We are looking for people who share our values, challenge ordinary thinking, and push the pace of innovation while building a future for themselves and Snowflake.

How do you want to make your impact?

For jobs located in the United States, please visit the job posting on the Snowflake Careers Site for salary and benefits information: careers.snowflake.com http://careers.snowflake.com

Bank: snowflake-db/resume.toml, variant `snowflake_db`. A pre-edit copy is in bank_backup/resume.toml.pre_sfdb.
Built PDF: snowflake-db/out/Alex_Rivera_Resume_snowflake_db.pdf, copied to ./resume.pdf. check.py passes (1 page, 2.75 in empty at the bottom).

## Chosen and why
- **tinykv leads (3 bullets).** A Raft key-value store with a WAL is the closest match to "FoundationDB key-value store (FDB storage, FDB Performance)", "Large-scale distributed systems" and "Software frameworks for stability and performance testing". It is also the only dated, most recent project.
  - core: storage plus replication (as in the bank).
  - chaos_short: a shortened copy of `chaos` with the same facts. "back through the log" was cut because it left a 4-word last line.
  - perf_conc: a reworded copy of `perf` with the same facts. "1 to 64 clients" became "as concurrent clients grew from 1 to 64" to answer "concurrency".
- **Shopline (3 bullets).** This is the Java evidence (Spring Boot, JUnit), plus a PostgreSQL schema (database systems), AWS ("cloud infrastructure, AWS") and software-engineering practice (tests, CI).
  - api_conc: a reworded copy of `api`, which now names optimistic locking as "concurrency control".
- **throttle (2 bullets).** Algorithms ("Knowledge of data structures and algorithms"), plus atomic shared state across 3 instances (concurrency, distributed).
- **DocQA (2 bullets, last).** Off-topic for a DB engine, but it shows latency work and benchmarking. It also fits the JD's "experimental mindset" and "AI-native" intro. It fills space the bank has no better bullet for. It is the first thing to cut.
- **Experience.** The Data Analyst Intern SQL pipelines are the closest thing to "big data" / data processing. I shortened that bullet in the bank (shared by all variants) to fix a 1-word last line. It now reads "for daily reporting; built dashboards for 3 planning KPIs", which drops "used in weekly planning". Restore it from the backup if you prefer the old wording.
- **Skills.** I added new groups built only from items already in the bank: lang_sfdb (Java first, TypeScript dropped), db_sfdb, cloud_sfdb (Kubernetes dropped because it is unrelated to the JD), and test_sfdb (labelled with the JD's "Stability & Performance Testing"). The `dist` line is reused as is. The AI/LLM line is left out.
- **Availability line on.** The JD lists start/end date options and a 12-week minimum. The line also shows enrollment during the internship.

- DocQA's AI skills line: unrelated to database engineering.
- Kubernetes, TypeScript, FastAPI, WebSockets, pytest from the skills lines: not relevant to this JD.
- kv.perf, kv.chaos and shop.api originals: replaced by same-fact variants (one fact appears once).

## If a reviewer pushes back
- "Not enough Java": the Shopline title line could say "in Java" if Alex confirms the project is Java (Spring Boot plus JUnit strongly suggest it, but the bank never says so). That would raise Java to 2 mentions.
- "Too much whitespace": the bank has no more relevant true bullets. Options: (a) Alex adds facts, e.g. tinykv implementation details on goroutines/locks, which would also cover "multi-threading", or (b) restore the AI/LLM skills line (weakly relevant).
- "DocQA is noise": remove it. The page still passes, with more whitespace.
- Gaps to prepare honest interview answers for: C++, Java version, multi-threading (threads specifically), operating systems and data structures coursework, big data, Spark/Hadoop, query execution/optimization, compilers, transaction processing, open source.

"acknowledged" became "acked" to avoid a 2-word last line. A real fix needs a power-loss or fsync-off control run, which the bank doesn't have (see gaps).

| Teamwork | **No evidence.** All projects look solo |
| Full-time in designated office | "full-time (12 weeks)". Based in Seattle with no mention of relocating to Menlo Park. 12 weeks is the minimum; we recommend 16 |

## 4. Bullets I can't follow or don't believe
- **"Lost 0 of 10,000 acknowledged writes across 50 SIGKILL faults"**: SIGKILL kills the process, but the OS page cache survives. So this doesn't show that fsync works. A test with fsync turned off might also lose 0 writes. It needs a control run or a power-loss or disk-fault style test.
- **"Scaled … from 80 to 2,400 writes/s as concurrent clients grew from 1 to 64 via group commit"**: Two effects are mixed together here: more clients and group commit. There is no with/without comparison and no hardware stated. Were all 3 nodes on one laptop? 2,400 writes/s is modest without that context.
- **"250 ms median leader failover"**: This mostly depends on the election timeout chosen. Over how many trials, and what was the p99?
- **"enforced a shared 1,000 req/s limit exactly under load"**: "Exactly" is a big claim. What load, measured over what window, and with what error?
- **"Designed 25 REST endpoints"**: An endpoint count says nothing about results. The project also has no date, which is true of three of the four projects.
- **"Recall@5 from 65% to 95%"**: The test set has only 60 queries and 12 configs were tried, so this is probably overfit. It also has nothing to do with this role.
- **tinykv dated Oct 2026**: It's very recent and the other projects have no dates, so I'd check how well the candidate really owns this code.

## 5. Interview questions
1. In tinykv, walk me through a write from the client to the ack. When exactly do you fsync? How would you prove that a write acked before a crash survives, given that SIGKILL leaves the page cache intact?
2. Separate out group commit's share of the 80 → 2,400 writes/s gain. What was the throughput at 64 clients with group commit off, and where was the bottleneck?
3. Have you taken or self-studied operating systems? Explain what happens on `write()` vs. `fsync()`, and how you would build a thread-safe structure like your WAL buffer in Java or C++.

## 6. Suggested changes (highest impact first)
1. **Close the coursework gap.** List Operating Systems, Data Structures and Software Engineering if they were taken in the BS or MS (or are planned before summer). OS is required, and missing it can get the resume filtered out automatically.
2. **Show systems work in Java or C++.** Add concurrency work in Java (thread pools, locks, `java.util.concurrent`) or port a piece of tinykv. Name the Java version (17 or 21).
3. **Make the tinykv numbers defensible.** State the setup (machines vs. localhost), add a control run with group commit off, and add a power-loss or fsync-disabled test that shows the WAL actually matters.
4. **Add teamwork evidence.** Describe a team project, a code review, or the cross-team work in the analyst internship. An open-source contribution would cover teamwork and a bonus item at once.
5. **Replace DocQA with database-internals work,** such as a B-tree or LSM, a query executor, or a SQL parser. Date every project and say you will relocate to Menlo Park.

## 1. 10-second impression
This is a backend/distributed-systems MS CS student (3.9 GPA, graduating Dec 2027) who also has hands-on RAG/LLM evaluation work. All the substance is in four personal projects; the only job is a 5-month data analyst internship. Match: **medium-strong**. CS fundamentals and the AI requirement are clearly covered. ## 2. Move to next round
**Yes.** The projects are technically deep and backed by measured numbers, and the DocQA project directly covers the JD's LLM/model-evaluation requirement. The weak spots (all solo work, no responsible-AI signal, work authorization not stated) are things a phone screen can check.

## 3. Hard requirements vs. evidence
| JD requirement | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Enrolled BS/MS, graduating Dec 2027 – Jun 2028 | "Master of Science in Computer Science … Expected Dec 2027". This is inside the window, but only just. |
| Less than 2 years full-time relevant experience | Met: the only job is "Data Analyst Intern, Jan 2024 – May 2024". There is an unexplained gap between the BS ending in Jun 2024 and the MS start date, which isn't listed. |
| CS fundamentals (DS, algorithms, design patterns) | "Coursework: Algorithms, Distributed Systems, Databases"; "4 rate-limiting algorithms … behind one interface"; Raft "leader election, log replication" |
| One or more languages/tools | "Java, Go, Python, SQL, TypeScript". Java and Go are clearly used in the projects. TypeScript has no project behind it. |
| AI foundations (model evaluation, LLM APIs) | "Benchmarked 12 retrieval configurations on a 60-query test set, raising Recall@5 from 65% to 95%"; "LLM evaluation harnesses" |
| Responsible AI (fairness, privacy, safety) | **No evidence** |
| Problem-solving and collaboration | Problem-solving is strong (tinykv chaos harness). Collaboration: **no evidence**. Every project reads as solo. |
| Written and verbal communication | **No evidence** beyond the resume being clear |
| Time management / adaptability | **No evidence** |
| Leadership / teaching / community (plus) | **No evidence** |
| US work authorization, no sponsorship ever | **No evidence.** The resume doesn't say. This is a hard gate for this role. |
| Based in SF, in office 3 days a week | The candidate is in Seattle, WA. Relocation is provided, so this is fine if they're willing to move. |

## 4. Bullets I can't follow or don't believe
- **"enforced a shared 1,000 req/s limit exactly under load"**: "Exactly" is a red flag. Distributed limiters always have some error at window edges. I'd want to see the measured over-admission rate.
- **"raising Recall@5 from 65% to 95%" on "a 60-query test set" after "12 retrieval configurations"**: If you pick the best of 12 configs on the same 60 queries, you are tuning on the test set. A 30-point gain on n=60 is probably overfit unless there was a held-out split.
- **"Cut p50 answer latency from 9.0s to 3.5s by caching embeddings and removing a redundant retrieval call"**: Removing a redundant call is fixing your own bug, not optimizing. I can't tell how much of the gain came from which change.
- **"Scaled a 3-node cluster from 80 to 2,400 writes/s via group commit"**: 30x is believable if the baseline did one fsync per write. Without the hardware and batch size, the number has no anchor.
- **Shopline (all three bullets)**: Endpoints, coverage and a deploy, but no result. Nobody uses it, there's no load number, and nothing explains why optimistic locking mattered. It reads like a tutorial project.
- **Skills listed with no supporting work**: Kubernetes, gRPC, WebSockets, TypeScript, "tool-calling agents" and "Go race detector" don't appear in any bullet.
- **No dates on any project**: I can't tell what's recent, or what the candidate did between Jun 2024 and the MS.

## 5. Interview questions
1. "In tinykv, walk me through a SIGKILL that happens after the leader appends to its log but before a majority acks. What does the client see, and how does your harness tell 'lost' apart from 'never acknowledged'?"
2. "For DocQA, how did you build the 60 queries and their relevance labels? Did you choose the winning configuration on the same set you report 95% on?"
3. "Imagine your support-ticket Q&A ran on real Airbnb guest messages. What privacy or safety problems would you design for? Also, tell me about a time you built something with other people and disagreed on the approach."

## 6. Suggested changes (highest impact first)
1. **State work authorization** in the header (for example, "US work authorized, no sponsorship required"). If this isn't clear, the resume gets filtered out before any technical screen.
2. **Add one collaborative or people-facing item**: a team project, TA or mentoring role, open-source PR, or hackathon. Right now every line is solo, and the JD explicitly asks for collaboration, communication and leadership.
3. **Fix the DocQA evaluation claim**: report results on a held-out split, or rephrase the bullet. Then add one bullet on responsible AI, such as PII redaction in tickets, refusing to answer when retrieval confidence is low, or hallucination checks. This covers a JD requirement that currently has zero evidence.
4. **Replace or shorten Shopline with something user-facing** (TypeScript/React plus a backend), or give Shopline a measured result. Airbnb's example intern projects are full-stack product features, and this resume has no UI work.
5. **Add dates to the projects, explain the 2024–MS gap, and trim unused skills** (Kubernetes, gRPC, WebSockets) so every listed skill has a bullet behind it. Change "exactly" to the measured error figure.

   4. Optional: add a year to each project so the parsed projects have dates.

VERDICT: pass

**1. 10-second impression**
This is an MS CS student (graduating Dec 2027) who leans toward backend and distributed systems. The resume has Raft, a rate limiter, a Spring Boot backend and a RAG Q&A project, plus one 5-month Data Analyst internship that involved SQL pipelines and dashboards. **Match: medium.** The engineering is solid and the GenAI/search work maps well to the JD's projects. But the data-engineering experience is thin (one bullet), and nothing shows interest in finance or trading.

**2. Move to the next round: yes.** The JD's example projects are a metrics dashboard, GenAI analysis of trading data and advanced search, and this resume has real evidence for all three. The one open item to confirm in the screen call is that the candidate will work in the NYC office.

**3. Hard requirements**
- **Graduation between Dec 2027 and May 2028:** "Master of Science in Computer Science … Expected Dec 2027". The date is in the window. The JD says "undergraduate graduation" and this is a master's, which is probably fine but needs a check with recruiting.
- **Major in Computer Science / Data Engineering:** "Master of Science in Computer Science". The undergrad degree is "Information Systems".
- **Strong communication and analytical skills:** The analytical side is covered indirectly: "benchmarking 12 retrieval configurations", "dashboards for 3 KPIs used in weekly planning". There is **no evidence** of communication: no presenting, writing, client contact or teamwork.
- **June–August 2027 time frame:** "Summer 2027 internship, full-time (12 weeks)". Matches.
- **In office in NYC, Monday through Friday:** **No evidence.** The candidate is in Seattle, WA, and the resume doesn't mention relocating.

**4. Bullets I can't follow or don't believe**
- "Raised Recall@5 from 65% to 95%…": The resume doesn't say how big the eval set or the ticket set is, or where the data came from. A 30-point gain on an unnamed benchmark could come from 20 hand-written questions.
- "Held 3 gateway instances to a shared 1,000 req/s limit **exactly**": "Exactly" makes me suspicious. What was measured, over what window, and how much did it overshoot?
- "Scaled a 3-node cluster from 80 to 2,400 writes/s via group commit": A 30× gain is believable with fsync batching. Still, the resume doesn't give the hardware, the batch size, or what happened to latency.
- "Added cart, order and inventory features to an e-commerce platform": This reads like a team product, but it's a personal project. Whose platform is it, and does anyone use it?
- "Wrote SQL pipelines joining 3 operational systems… dashboards for 3 KPIs": This is the only real work experience and the bullet that matters most for this role. It gives no data volume, tools, schedule, users or outcome. "WebSockets" appears in skills but no bullet backs it up, and the JD stresses real-time data.

**5. Interview questions**
1. On DocQA: how did you build the eval set behind the 65%→95% Recall@5 figure? How many queries were there and who labeled them? What did the winning configuration change?
2. At Example Logistics: walk me through one pipeline end to end. What were the source systems and data volume, how was it scheduled, what broke, and how did you find out?
3. Say we want to show clients live loan prices and trade activity on a dashboard. How would you design ingestion through to display, and how would you handle late or duplicate quotes?

**6. Suggested changes (biggest effect on the decision first)**
1. Add a line on location: "Relocating to NYC for Summer 2027; available in-office M–F." Without it, a Seattle address on an in-office NYC role is an easy reason to reject.
2. Expand the Data Analyst internship into 2–3 bullets with tools (warehouse, scheduler, BI tool), data scale, who used the output, and one result such as time saved or a decision it changed. This is the most relevant experience on the page.
3. Reorder the projects so data and GenAI come first: DocQA first, and cut or shorten throttle. Use the space for a data project, ideally real-time or streaming on public market data, which would also back up the WebSockets skill.
4. Give DocQA some scope: corpus size, eval-set size, what the 12 configurations varied, and what the data was.
5. Add one sign of interest in fintech or trading, whether a project, a course or a single line. The JD is clearly looking for people "interested in fintech and electronic trading."

VERDICT: yes

Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

 ABOUT THE JOB 

 We are seeking a Machine Learning Intern for Summer 2027! This is a paid, in-person, 12-week internship. On Maritime Digital Production, you will apply machine learning to the data that defines and tracks how our maritime vehicles are built: 3D CAD models with embedded manufacturing information, engineering drawings, and production and quality records. You will own a prototype from problem statement to demonstration, working with the engineers who author the models, the developers who build our manufacturing systems, and the technicians who build and inspect our vehicles.

 WHAT YOU’LL DO 

- Receive problem statements, guidelines, requirements, and reporting milestones

- Frame a manufacturing data problem as an ML task, build a labeled dataset from CAD models, drawings, or production records, and define how success will be measured

- Train and evaluate models (for example, graph or vision models on 3D geometry and drawings, or language and vision-language models for document understanding) and compare them against simple baselines

- Build the pipeline around the model: data extraction, preprocessing, evaluation, and a review step where engineers confirm or correct predictions

- Independently perform experiments and trade studies, and generate solutions for approval

- Test, verify, and demonstrate your prototype with the engineers who would use it, and document results and limits

 REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS   

- Must be pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Data Science, Mathematics, Statistics, Electrical Engineering, or a related field. 

- Must be returning to school at the end of the internship to continue academic studies for at least one quarter or semester.

- Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export-controlled information or facilities; U.S. clearance eligibility may be required depending on program.

- Ability to complete an in-person 12-week internship in Santa Ana, CA, in summer 2027.

 PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS   

- Proficiency in Python and experience with a deep learning framework such as PyTorch or TensorFlow

- Coursework or project experience in machine learning, with a foundation in data structures, algorithms, calculus, probability, and statistics

- Experience in computer vision, graph neural networks, or natural language processing, including large language or vision-language models

- Experience designing experiments, analyzing results, and building end-to-end ML pipelines on real, messy datasets

- Familiarity with Git, Docker, Linux, and GPU or cloud training environments

- C++ or CUDA experience

- Experience using AI coding tools while critically validating their output

- Exposure to CAD, 3D geometry, engineering drawings, or manufacturing data

- Prior projects, research, or open-source work you can show, and strong technical communication skills

 US Hourly Range 
 $42 — $60 USD 

 The salary range for this role is an estimate based on a wide range of compensation factors, inclusive of base salary only. Actual salary offer may vary based on (but not limited to) work experience, education and/or training, critical skills, and/or business considerations. Highly competitive equity grants are included in the majority of full time offers; and are considered part of Anduril's total compensation package. Additionally, Anduril offers top-tier benefits for full-time employees, including:   

  

 Benefits 

 At Anduril, we invest in our people. Our comprehensive, competitive benefits package (available at little to no cost to employees) ensures you’re supported in health, recovery, and whatever comes next.  For more information, Explore Our Benefits . 

  

 Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams 

 Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. We've observed a rise in sophisticated phishing and fraudulent schemes where individuals impersonate Anduril representatives, luring job seekers with false interviews or job offers. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

 To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

- 
 No Financial Requests:  Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.

- Please always verify communications: 

- Direct from Anduril: If you receive an email from one of our recruiters, it will only come from an @anduril.com address.

- Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com . 

- 
 Exercise Caution with Unsolicited Outreach:  If you receive any communication that appears suspicious, contains grammatical errors, or makes unusual requests, do not engage. Always confirm the sender's email domain is @anduril.com before providing any personal information or clicking on links.

- 
 What to Do If You Suspect Fraud:  Should you encounter any questionable or fraudulent outreach claiming to be from Anduril, please report it immediately to  contact@anduril.com . Your proactive caution is invaluable in protecting your personal information and upholding the security and trustworthiness of our recruitment efforts.

  

 Data Privacy 

 To view Anduril's candidate data privacy policy, please visit https://anduril.com/applicant-privacy-notice/ .   

  

 By submitting your application, you consent to Anduril Industries using a third-party service provider to conduct pre-employment risk, integrity, and due diligence screening and assessing potential risks as part of your application process. This third-party service provider provides risk-intelligence services that may include analysis of sanctions and watchlists, adverse media, public-record information, and other lawful open-source or commercial data sources. This third-party service provider does not act as a consumer reporting agency.
